publicationHistory.note: Compiled by William Walker of Spartanburg, South Carolina; printed by Nathan Whiting, New Haven, Connecticut. i-xxxii + 216 pp. This is the Work's true origin (w_SoH's firstEditionYear) - a separate fact from this Edition's own 1854 identifier year.
Two distinct 1847 editions were printed, both in Philadelphia.

"New Edition, Thoroughly Revised and Much Enlarged." Published by E.W. Miller, Philadelphia. xxxii + 336 pp. (original pagination skips 217-248). This is the edition Hymnary.org and CCEL both index, and the one this Tunebook File's song data comes from.

University Press of Kentucky, with an introduction by Glenn C. Wilcox. A facsimile of this 1854 printing specifically - Wilcox edited this reprint's introduction, not the original 1854 tunes, and is not the Work's compiler (that is William Walker; an earlier version of this Library's Work record had this backwards, misattributing the Work's own responsibilityStatement to Wilcox).

scholarlyRecord.editorialHistory: Walker reported 500,000 copies of Southern Harmony sold by 1866, across all editions combined, per the Southern Cultures review of the 1993 facsimile (cited below). Southern Harmony singings using this book specifically continue today, most notably the annual Benton, Kentucky singing.

scholarlyRecord.historicalNotes: The song index in this file was built from a CCEL/Hymnary.org comparison dataset Kevin provided, not transcribed by hand. That source's own page-numbering convention differs from this suite's: it uses a bare number for the top tune on a split page and a 'b' suffix for the bottom tune, with no 't' suffix at all - converted here to this suite's own t/b convention (bare number reserved for a page with only one tune). Verified against three failure modes before import: no split page had more than two tunes, no page had a lone 'b' entry with no bare counterpart, and the 335 real (canonical) tune count matches published sources exactly. Seven rows in the source data were alternate CCEL headings for tunes already counted once (e.g. "WOODSTOCK" as an alternate heading for "GOSPEL TRUMPET" on 271t) - these are preserved as historicalNote text on the correct song rather than counted as separate songs.
